correctness.rationale: A regular n-gon difference body has exactly N=n (even n) or N=2n (odd n) evenly spaced extreme directions, with known amplitude; this is proved by antipodal vertex pairs. Its normalized width has an absolutely convergent cosine Fourier series whose coefficients were explicitly integrated. Product orthogonality selects exactly common frequencies j*lcm(N,M). Direct cell-splitting yields the exact autocorrelation R(t), and differentiation gives the strictly negative expression [t sin(2h-t)-(2h-t) sin t]/(4h) for 0<t<h, by monotonicity of sin(x)/x. This establishes all global extrema and their equality classes, not only critical points. Minkowski width additivity transfers the result to any positive weights. Exact endpoint identities and asymptotics were independently re-derived and direct polygon-vertex numerical integration passed in CHECK.py. No finite experiment substitutes for these analytic universal steps.

originality.rationale: The inspected Akiyama–Kamae 2022 work has a general pairwise shadow-moment formula, which already implies that arbitrary two-polygon mixed moments are computable; that generality is expressly excluded from novelty. The present theorem instead classifies global and unique relative-rotation minimizers of width variance for every ordered pair of regular polygon side counts and all positive Minkowski weights. Its exact lcm collapse, parity-switch, strict phase optimization and O(L^-4) signed extrema require a specialized nontrivial Fourier selection and monotonic periodic autocorrelation proof not present in the inspected theorems. value.rationale: The geometry problem is to choose the relative rotation of two given regular shapes to minimize directional thickness variation in their Minkowski sum while keeping their mean thickness fixed. The precise sign of the best alignment has an arithmetic lcm/parity dependence: peak-aligned square and octagon already have strictly negative covariance, an effect not captured by individual width variances. The universal closed-form K_L and sharp O(L^-4) extremal decay measure how geometric features at incommensurate symmetries interact. This is a meaningful complete sharp two-body classification, not merely a known one-polygon variance substitution.
